title: GitHub OAuth login for the Todo app
constraints: Do not change existing Todo CRUD business logic (status transitions, completedAt handling, period normalization, parent/child rules, reorder logic) -- only add an ownership/authorization layer around it.
No hardcoded CLIENT_SECRET anywhere in code -- must come from process.env.GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET only, no fallback literal.
Do not report complete while incomplete.
designNotes: Hand-rolled OAuth (Authorization Code flow), not NextAuth, so the exact required routes (/auth/github, /auth/github/callback) match without fighting a library's own routing conventions. DB-backed sessions (Session model, SHA-256-hashed token in DB, raw token in an httpOnly cookie) so logout can truly delete server-side state, not just clear a client cookie. OAuth `state` via a short-lived httpOnly cookie (double-submit pattern), no extra signing secret needed. Callback route calls two isolated functions (exchangeCodeForToken, fetchGithubUser) in lib/github-oauth.ts so tests can fetch-mock GitHub's responses -- same pattern already used throughout this codebase's tests, no real GitHub App needed for automated tests. A real GitHub OAuth App (real CLIENT_ID/CLIENT_SECRET, browser click-through) is required for a full manual end-to-end login test, which the assistant cannot do itself -- this is flagged as a known verification gap, not silently skipped.

stories.title: Data model: User, Session, Todo.userId + migration script
stories.description: Add User and Session models to prisma/schema.prisma, make Todo.userId a required field, and provide a migration script for any pre-existing userId-less Todo documents.
acceptanceCriteria: prisma/schema.prisma defines a User model (id, githubId unique, username, avatarUrl, createdAt, updatedAt) and a Session model (id, tokenHash unique, userId, expiresAt, createdAt) with a relation from Session to User
Todo model gets a required `userId String @db.ObjectId` field (no default), plus an index on userId
`npx prisma db push` succeeds against the local test MongoDB with the new schema

scripts/migrate-add-user-id.ts exists: given a github username, finds/requires that User exists, and assigns all Todo documents missing userId to that user's id; run and documented in docs/GITHUB_OAUTH_SETUP.md

lib/session.ts exports createSession(userId) (returns raw token, stores SHA-256 hash + expiresAt in DB), getSessionUser(token) (hash-lookup, expiry check, returns User or null), deleteSession(token) (deletes the DB row); unit/integration tested
stories.notes: Verified: schema.prisma User/Session/Todo.userId pushed to Atlas via npx prisma db push (real run, output captured). lib/session.ts has 5 passing tests (valid token, hash-not-raw-token, unknown token, expiry+cleanup, deleteSessionByToken). scripts/migrate-add-user-id.ts refactored to export a testable migrateOrphanedTodosToUser() function; tests/scripts/migrate-add-user-id.test.ts raw-inserts a userId-less Todo (bypassing the now-required schema field) and proves the migration assigns it correctly while leaving already-owned todos untouched (2 tests).

stories.title: GitHub OAuth routes (/auth/github, /auth/github/callback)
stories.description: Implement the OAuth Authorization Code flow: redirect to GitHub, handle the callback (state verification, code exchange, profile fetch, user upsert, session cookie).
acceptanceCriteria: GET /auth/github sets a random `oauth_state` httpOnly cookie and redirects (302) to https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, state, and scope=read:user query params
lib/github-oauth.ts exports exchangeCodeForToken(code) and fetchGithubUser(accessToken) as isolated functions calling GitHub's token and user endpoints respectively, so tests can fetch-mock them
GET /auth/github/callback rejects (400) if the `state` query param doesn't match the `oauth_state` cookie, or if `code` is missing

On a valid callback, upserts a User by githubId (creates on first login, updates username/avatarUrl on subsequent logins), creates a Session, sets the session cookie (httpOnly, sameSite=lax), clears the oauth_state cookie, and redirects (302) to /
CLIENT_SECRET is read only from process.env.GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET, no literal fallback; missing env var fails loudly at the exchange call, not silently
Integration tests fetch-mock GitHub's token + user endpoints and exercise: successful login (User+Session created, cookie set), state mismatch (400), missing code (400)
stories.notes: Verified: tests/api/auth.test.ts (7 tests) covers missing code->400, state mismatch->400, no state cookie->400, successful login (fetch-mocked GitHub token+user endpoints) creating User+Session+cookie and that the new cookie actually authenticates a follow-up /api/todos call, and second-login-same-githubId updates rather than duplicates. Live-verified against a REAL registered GitHub OAuth App (real GITHUB_CLIENT_ID/SECRET appeared in .env): GET /auth/github redirects to a correctly-formed https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize URL with the real client_id, dynamic redirect_uri matching the actual running port, random state, scope=read:user, and sets a matching httpOnly oauth_state cookie.

stories.title: Logout
stories.description: Fully delete server-side session state on logout, not just the cookie.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /auth/logout deletes the matching Session row from the DB (looked up by the cookie's token hash) and clears the session cookie
After logout, a request with the old cookie value is treated as unauthenticated (401 on API routes)
Tested: log in (create session) -> logout -> subsequent API call with the old cookie returns 401
stories.notes: Verified: tests/api/auth.test.ts logout test creates a session, confirms it authenticates, logs out, confirms the Session row is gone from the DB and the same old cookie now gets 401.

stories.title: Route protection: unauthenticated users cannot reach the todo list
stories.description: Gate the main page behind a session check; provide a login page.
acceptanceCriteria: app/login/page.tsx renders a "GitHub로 로그인" button/link to /auth/github
app/page.tsx (server component) checks the session cookie via lib/session.ts; unauthenticated requests are redirected to /login (not just shown an error)
Authenticated requests render the existing TodoApp UI, now also showing the logged-in user's github username/avatar and a logout control
This does not alter TodoApp's or any child component's existing CRUD behavior -- only adds the session gate at the page level and a user/logout header
stories.notes: Verified: app/login/page.tsx renders the GitHub login link. app/page.tsx redirects unauthenticated requests to /login (live-verified via curl: 307 to /login) and unauthenticated /api/todos returns 401 (live-verified). UserHeader added without touching TodoApp/TodoBoard/TodoCard CRUD logic.

stories.title: API authorization: 401 when unauthenticated, ownership scoping when authenticated
stories.description: Every /api/todos* route requires a valid session and scopes all reads/writes to the session user's own todos, without changing the existing CRUD/validation logic itself.
acceptanceCriteria: GET/POST /api/todos, PATCH/DELETE /api/todos/:id, and PATCH /api/todos/reorder all return 401 if there is no valid session (no cookie, or cookie doesn't match any non-expired Session)
GET /api/todos only returns todos owned by the session user (userId filter merged into the existing where-clause logic, not replacing it)
POST /api/todos sets userId from the session, not from the request body (a client-supplied userId in the body is ignored)

PATCH/DELETE /api/todos/:id on a todo owned by a different user returns 404 (not 403, to avoid confirming existence) -- existing todo-not-found and malformed-id handling from the prior implementation is unchanged
PATCH /api/todos/reorder rejects (404) if any id in orderedIds is not owned by the session user
All existing (pre-auth) CRUD/validation tests still pass, updated only to authenticate as a test user first -- proving the underlying business logic was not altered
New tests cover: 401 without a session, cross-user 404 on PATCH/DELETE/reorder, GET only returning the caller's own todos
stories.notes: Verified via 29 tests in tests/api/todos.test.ts (401 on every route without a session, GET only returns the caller own todos, POST ignores a client-supplied userId, cross-user 404 on PATCH/DELETE/reorder, cross-user parent-link rejected with 400) plus the pre-existing CRUD/validation tests updated only to authenticate first -- all passing unchanged, proving the underlying business logic was not altered.

stories.title: Setup guide + .env.example
stories.description: Document how to register a GitHub OAuth App and configure the environment, and how to run the userId migration.
acceptanceCriteria: .env.example exists at the repo root listing GITHUB_CLIENT_ID, GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET (with a comment that it must never be committed with a real value), and the existing DATABASE_URL/MONGODB_URI pattern, consistent with the current .env usage

docs/GITHUB_OAUTH_SETUP.md walks through: creating a GitHub OAuth App (Settings > Developer settings > OAuth Apps), setting the Authorization callback URL to match /auth/github/callback, filling in .env, and running the scripts/migrate-add-user-id.ts migration
No real secret values appear anywhere in the committed docs or .env.example
stories.notes: .env.example and docs/GITHUB_OAUTH_SETUP.md written; no real secret values in either. Setup guide explicitly tells the user to match the callback URL to whatever port npm run dev actually lands on (ports vary here since 3000+ are often occupied on this machine), since GitHub OAuth requires an exact match.
